title: Windows from the same parent application, including different web apps from the same browser, all show the same media preview and controls
line: When a browser plays media, the task tooltips of its other windows and web apps no longer show the media controls of the playing one.
explanation: A browser exposes one media player for all its windows, and the task manager looks that player up by process, so every ungrouped window tooltip of the browser (including its web apps) got the same media controls and volume slider. The grouped tooltip already used the window titles to pick the playing window, but the single-window tooltip never did. The single tooltip now checks whether any window of the same process has the track in its title; if one does, only that window shows the controls. If none does, nothing changes.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: show media controls only on the window playing

Ungrouped task tooltips showed the media controls on every window of the
same process, such as all windows and web apps of a browser. Now, if one
of its windows has the track in its title, only that one shows them.

BUG: 504234

media.caption: Chrome, ungrouped: the tooltip of the quiet window shows the 'Test Tone' controls playing in the other window
Same setup with the fix: the quiet window's tooltip has no media controls

reviews.text: Extending the task manager's title-based track matching from grouped tooltips to ungrouped single-window tooltips is the right Plasma-side approach given browsers only expose one MPRIS player per process. However, the patch misses the media preview (album art) for PWAs, introduces a grouped-tooltip regression when playerData.track is empty, and mismatches raw display titles against stripped titles.
changes: Fix albumArtImage.available in ToolTipInstance.qml so non-WebBrowser PWAs also hide the playing window's album art (showing their own PipeWire thumbnail instead) when root.hasTrackInATitle is true and !root.titleIncludesTrack, and verify with a PWA/non-WebBrowser desktop entry and media that provides artUrl.

Guard against empty playerData.track in both groupToolTipListView.hasTrackInATitle (ToolTipDelegate.qml) and ToolTipInstance.titleIncludesTrack (ToolTipInstance.qml); because the patch removed the albumArtImage.available gate from playerController and volumeControls, String.includes("") now evaluates to true and duplicates controls on every window of a grouped tooltip whenever track metadata is empty.

Match against the same title string in hasTrackInATitle and titleIncludesTrack (e.g. raw display rather than mixing Qt.DisplayRole with stripped root.title), otherwise a track name occurring after a dash separator sets hasTrackInATitle to true while titleIncludesTrack is false for all windows and hides controls everywhere.

reviews.text: Reusing the grouped tooltip's title-matching heuristic for single tooltips is a reasonable direction, and the rig shows the controls leaving the quiet Chrome window. But the bug is about PWAs sharing both the media preview and the controls, and the preview part is untouched. In ToolTipInstance.qml albumArtImage.available only checks titleIncludesTrack for groups or for launchers in the WebBrowser category. A PWA has its own launcher, so every quiet PWA window still swaps its thumbnail for the playing track's album art. The test tone had no art and no PWA was used, so this never showed. The notes also admit that when no title contains the track, every window keeps the controls exactly as before. That is the reporter's case for many web apps, and the fix ends up behaving differently by browser and site.
changes: Apply the same rule to the album-art preview in single tooltips: when another window of the process has the track in its title (hasTrackInATitle), show the art only where titleIncludesTrack, whatever the launcher's category.
Verify with an actual PWA (separate .desktop launcher) plus a normal browser window, using media that has artwork, and include before/after shots of a quiet PWA tooltip.

Decide and implement the no-title-match case for processes with several windows (e.g. show controls and art on none, or only on one well-defined window) so the bug is closed rather than only improved for title-tagged sites, or else downgrade to CCBUG.
Call out in the commit message that grouped tooltips no longer require album art for the title-matched window's controls, or drop that change.
